clue.text: Politicians being moderate left party having upset comrades — about time?

parts.note: a social is a party or informal gathering

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the letter for time
upset means the letters of comrades are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of whether politicians of the moderate left, at a party, have fallen out with their comrades over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the comrades and 'about' wraps those letters round T, producing DEMOCRA_S around the T; the party is the first word, not a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Social democrats are politicians of the moderate, reformist left rather than the hard left.

clue.text: Give comfort to one easily fooled, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is chosen for how it is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible person, easily taken in

explanation.surface: Advice to console someone who has been gullible.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour is to aid and comfort someone in distress, a slightly old-fashioned verb.

clue.text: Somewhere to sleep on holiday around sea, taking lead

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means around or approximately

indicators.note: taking means the sea's letters take in the metal's symbol

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: A traveller looking for a place to sleep near the sea, taking charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, not leadership, so its symbol PB goes into MED.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp bed is a folding portable bed, used when camping or as a spare.

clue.text: Historic Premier League clash — mood changed

indicators.note: changed means the letters of the three words are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A football report: a Premier League match, and the mood shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier League' looks like football; 'Premier' belongs to the definition, a prime minister. Alec Douglas-Home was UK Prime Minister in 1963-64.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alec Douglas-Home was a British Prime Minister in the 1960s, so a premier of history.

clue.text: Ireland's President Dave, real fashionable

indicators.note: fashionable is read as fashioned anew, so the letters of the two names are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone praising Ireland's president as a really stylish Dave.
explanation.walkthrough: Eamon de Valera was a founding figure of the Irish state and later its President.
explanation.definitionFit: Éamon de Valera served as President of Ireland from 1959 to 1973.

clue.text: Very short record

definitions.meaning: pronounced my-NEWT, the adjective means tiny or very small
... are the written record of a meeting, so to ... is to record

explanation.surface: A record that is very brief.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means tiny; the verb means to note officially, as in minutes of a meeting.

clue.text: What can give mariner cohesion under any conditions

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can give a new phrase when rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what keeps a sailor's crew together whatever the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means whatever happens, regardless of circumstances or weather.

clue.text: Store a herb around back of larder

indicators.note: around means the letters of a plus the herb go round the extra letter

parts.note: chives are an onion-flavoured herb

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of larder

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to keep a herb in the back of the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts R, the last letter of larder, inside A CHIVE, just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To archive is to store records or documents for keeping.

clue.text: Dark-coloured blemish one's reluctant to talk about

indicators.note: about means the word for timid goes around the blemish

parts.note: a shy person is reluctant to speak up
a wart is a small growth or blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: A dark mark on the skin that someone is embarrassed to mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy describes a dark complexion, so dark in colouring.

clue.text: Mobile accommodation for one following motorway in Irish county

indicators.note: in means those letters are placed inside the county name

parts.note: Cavan is a county in Ireland

indicators.note: following means the word for each comes after the motorway letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: A holiday home on wheels driving along a motorway in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A camper van is a vehicle fitted out for living in while travelling.

clue.text: Second tea or coffee

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
cha (or char) is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Choosing a second drink: tea or coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Round in shape, wearing ceremonial dress with a small alteration

indicators.note: a small alteration means one letter shifts its place in the word

parts.note: someone robed is dressed in formal robes

explanation.surface: Someone in ceremonial robes that are a touch rounded.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving R one place along turns ROBED into the new word.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbed means formed into an orb, a sphere, so circular or round.

clue.text: Performer of church ritual, mostly bombastic in inclination

indicators.note: in means the shortened word sits inside the lean

parts.note: a ship's list is its lean or inclination

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: turgid prose is pompous and overblown

explanation.surface: A clergyman whose services tend to be pompous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' is a ship's lean, not a preference; 'mostly' drops the last letter of the bombastic word.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgist leads or studies the forms of public worship in church.

clue.text: Devotee of Mao argued furiously with revolutionary doctor

indicators.note: furiously means the letters of argued are thrown about
revolutionary means the abbreviation turns right round

explanation.surface: A furious argument between a Maoist and a revolutionary doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' rearranges ARGUED to REDGUA; 'revolutionary' turns DR to RD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Guards were young militants mobilised by Mao during China's Cultural Revolution.

clue.text: Get by with railway company uniform

parts.note: to get by is to live, to survive

explanation.surface: Making do with the outfit issued by a railway firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A livery is a distinctive uniform or colour scheme worn by a company's staff or vehicles.

clue.text: Caught a heartless sports official in a good mood

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: a referee officiates at a match

explanation.surface: A referee caught in cheerful spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle E of REFEREE, leaving REFREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means without worries, light-hearted and happy.

clue.text: One may have a crush on this old Brazilian footballer around street

definitions.text: One may have a crush on this

indicators.note: around means the footballer's name goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: Pelé was the great Brazilian footballer of the 1950s-70s

explanation.surface: Fans with a crush on the old Brazilian star near the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crush' is grinding, not infatuation: a mortar's contents are crushed with a pestle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is the club-shaped tool used to crush substances in a mortar.

clue.text: Airborne troop's favourite high place

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A paratrooper's favourite lofty spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low wall along the edge of a roof, bridge or high balcony.

clue.text: Bowler — bad one keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the wrongdoer holds the letter within

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A poor bowler kept silent.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a bowler who spins the ball; 'Bowler' is not a hat here.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler who makes the ball turn.

clue.text: Honoured woman has quick drinks in pubs

indicators.note: in means the drinks go inside the pubs

parts.note: bars are pubs
a quick one is a quick drink, so quick ones are drinks

explanation.surface: A titled lady who downs swift drinks in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness holds a peerage, often a life peer honoured for public service.

clue.text: Serious attention given to living space

parts.note: to give ear is to give attention
a nest is a home or living space

explanation.surface: Serious thought given to housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in intent.

clue.text: Trail takes opposite directions back

indicators.note: takes means the trail takes the compass points inside it

parts.note: a spoor is the track or trail of an animal
N and S, north and south, are opposite compass points

explanation.surface: A path that turns back on itself in opposite directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person or event is to support it financially, which is to sponsor it.

clue.text: Oriental chant — part of Ottoman tradition

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chant that belongs to the customs of the Ottoman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred word or phrase repeated in Hindu and Buddhist meditation, from the East.

clue.text: Checks gallery to carry out restoration

parts.note: to rein in is to check, so reins are checks
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: An art gallery inspected before restoration work.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain, chiefly in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone or something to a former position.

clue.text: Control mechanism reduced user voltage

indicators.note: reduced means the two words are trimmed down to a short run of their letters

explanation.surface: A device that lowered the voltage for the user.
explanation.definitionFit: A servo is a servomechanism, an automatic device controlling motion by feedback.

clue.text: One of 1 Across perhaps to fix end of boxing match

parts.note: to pin is to fasten or fix
a KO, knockout, ends a boxing match

explanation.surface: A left-leaning politician trying to rig the result of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinko is a mildly derogatory term for someone left-of-centre; 'perhaps' marks it as one loose example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinko is a person with mild left-wing views, like a moderate leftist politician.

clue.text: Has meal entertained by sailors, being late

indicators.note: entertained by means the sailors take in the diner

parts.note: tars are sailors
to dine is to have a meal

explanation.surface: Dining with sailors and so turning up late.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is the state of being late or slow.

clue.text: Imbecile threatened every rider in competition

indicators.note: imbecile, used as an adjective meaning crazed, signals the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A fool menaced every horse rider in the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imbecile' looks like a noun subject but works as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-day eventer is a horse rider competing in dressage, cross-country and show jumping over three days.
